issues.legal_issue: A land-classification authority need not obtain independent evidence of assured irrigation when it forms its opinion by examining the relevant prescribed records and materials.
material_facts: The landholders challenged the classification of land as irrigated and argued that independent evidence of assured irrigation was required in addition to the relevant records.
The statutory process required the authority to examine specified land records and a village map, consider other records it found necessary, and make a local inspection where necessary.
issues.conclusion: The contention that independent evidence of assured irrigation was additionally required had no merit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4A of the U.P. Imposition of Ceiling on Land Holdings Act, 1960 directs the prescribed authority to examine the relevant khasras, the latest village map and other records it considers necessary, and permits local inspection where necessary. The authority must form its opinion on relevant material; no additional independent evidence of assured irrigation is required. The Act is social legislation intended to advance the objectives stated in its preamble.

predicates.ceiling_land_classification_proceeding: An authority is determining whether land is irrigated for the purpose of calculating a landholding ceiling.
predicates.authority_examined_relevant_records: The authority examined the relevant land records and other materials it considered necessary, and made a local inspection where it considered one necessary.
predicates.irrigation_facility_indicated_by_records: The materials examined by the authority indicated that irrigation facilities were available to the land.

issues.definition: When an authority classifies land in a ceiling proceeding after examining relevant records that indicate available irrigation facilities, separate independent evidence of irrigation is not required.

issues.legal_issue: Where irrigation facilities are available to an area and two crops are grown on part of it, the area may be classified as irrigated without proof that two crops were grown throughout it, absent material showing materially poorer soil in other portions.
material_facts: The landholders argued that two crops had to have been grown on the entire extent of the land for it to be classified as irrigated.
The relevant interpretation concerned land with irrigation facilities where two crops had been grown on only a portion of the land.
The Court reasoned that, absent material showing poor soil quality in other portions, the soil's quality and content could be presumed uniform throughout the land.
issues.conclusion: It was not necessary for two crops to have been grown on the entire extent of the land; growing two crops on a portion could support treating the entire area with irrigation facilities as irrigated.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 4A of the U.P. Imposition of Ceiling on Land Holdings Act, 1960, classification turns on irrigation availability and the land's actual or potential capacity to yield at least two crops in an agricultural year. The Court approved the interpretation in Kallu v. State of U.P., [1979] A.L.J. 1113, that crops grown on a portion of the irrigated area can satisfy the crop requirement for that area. In the absence of contrary material showing poorer soil in other portions, uniform soil quality and content may be presumed. The contrary views identified in Gasi Ram v. State of U.P., Surrinjpal Singh v. State of U.P., [1978] A.L.J. 1343, and Sitaram Tyagi v. State of U.P. were not accepted by the High Court, whose interpretation the Supreme Court upheld.

rule.if: ceiling_land_classification_proceeding and irrigation_available_to_area and two_crops_grown_on_part_of_area and not contrary_material_shows_soil_difference

predicates.ceiling_land_classification_proceeding: An authority is determining whether land is irrigated for the purpose of calculating a landholding ceiling.
predicates.irrigation_available_to_area: Irrigation facilities were available to the area being considered.
predicates.two_crops_grown_on_part_of_area: At least two crops were grown during a relevant agricultural year on some portion of the area with irrigation facilities.
predicates.contrary_material_shows_soil_difference: Evidence showed that other portions of the area had materially poorer soil quality or content.

issues.definition: In a ceiling-classification proceeding, when irrigation is available to an area and two crops are grown on part of it, the whole irrigated area may be treated as irrigated unless evidence shows a material soil difference in other portions.
